sections.label: AMLA public agencies established
sections.summary: AMLA established MUIS, ROMM and the Syariah Court to implement and administer the Act's provisions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: With AMLA, we saw the establishment of three public agencies − the Islamic Religious Council of Singapore (MUIS), the Registry of Muslim Marriages (ROMM) and the Syariah Court − dedicated to implement and administer the provisions of the Act.

sections.label: Marriage and minor marriage trends
sections.summary: Marriage numbers are rising while minor marriages decline, and younger-groom Muslim marriages show higher divorce rates.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Marriage numbers are on the rise while minor marriages − that is, marriages where at least one party was below 21 years of age at the time of marriage − have been in steady decline.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: For example, in the case of Muslim marriages involving younger grooms, the recent marriage cohorts have experienced one-and-a-half times the divorce rate compared to older grooms.

sections.label: Syariah Court child cases
sections.summary: About 64% of Syariah Court cases in the past five years involved a child under 21.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The Syariah Court's case records indicate that about 64% of its cases in the past five years involved at least one child of the marriage under 21 years old, with more than 85% of these involving at least one child aged under 14 years old.

sections.label: Syariah Court counselling programme
sections.summary: Since 2004, over 33,000 couples were counselled and almost half of these marriages were saved.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Since the Syariah Court's introduction of the Programme as an administrative requirement in 2004, over 33,000 couples have been counselled and almost half of these marriages have been saved.

sections.label: Wali solemnisation written consent
sections.summary: Couples wanting solemnisation by a wali must get written consent from the Kadi or Naib Kadi, who witnesses it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Couples who wish their marriage to be solemnised by a wali must seek written consent from the Kadi or Naib Kadi, who must be present as a witness at the solemnisation.

sections.label: Domicile requirement for applications
sections.summary: The third proposal specifies through section 35 of AMLA that at least one applicant must be domiciled or habitually resident in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The third proposal, therefore, is to specify through section 35 of AMLA that at least one of the parties making an application at the Syariah Court must be domiciled or habitually residing in Singapore.

sections.label: MUIS wakaf revenue disbursement
sections.summary: In 2017, MUIS disbursed $3.1 million of wakaf revenue to beneficiaries including mosques, madrasahs and Muslim organisations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: In 2017, MUIS disbursed $3.1 million of the revenue generated from our wakafs to various beneficiaries, such as mosques, madrasahs and Muslim organisations.

sections.label: Amending AMLA section 58
sections.summary: Section 58 of AMLA will be amended to expand the grounds for removing a trustee or mutawalli.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: To enable MUIS to better safeguard against the mismanagement of wakafs, we will amend section 58 of AMLA to expand the grounds on which a trustee or mutawalli can be removed.

sections.label: Removal for section 64(11) offence
sections.summary: A trustee or mutawalli can also be removed if convicted of an offence under section 64(11) of AMLA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The Bill, therefore, stipulates that a trustee or mutawalli can also be removed if convicted of any offence under section 64(11) of AMLA, which, among others, is committed when a mutawalli fails to furnish information or particulars as required by MUIS, or fails to allow MUIS' inspection of wakaf properties, accounts and records.

sections.label: New section 61 sinking fund
sections.summary: New section 61 seeks to allow MUIS to direct a portion of wakaf income towards a sinking fund.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Thirdly, new section 61 seeks to allow MUIS to direct a portion of the income of the wakaf towards a sinking fund, primarily for the upkeep and development of the wakaf.

sections.label: MBMF for mosque property
sections.summary: The MBMF can be tapped for purchase of new or additional land or property for mosques.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: For our mosques, we want to specify that the MBMF can be tapped on for the purchase of new or additional land or property for existing and future mosques.

sections.label: Protecting Muslim families and institutions
sections.summary: The amendments seek to better protect Muslim families, reinforce institutions and enhance asset management for the community.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The amendments we are proposing today seek to better protect Muslim families because they are the very building blocks of a strong and resilient community.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We want to reinforce our institutions so that they are effective in serving our community.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: And we want to enhance the management of our assets so that the community continues to benefit from them and prosper.

sections.label: Divorce and talak pronouncement
sections.summary: The amendment lets men apply for divorce as plaintiffs without pronouncing the talak, and asks whether the Syariah Court still requires talak and how frivolous pronouncements are discouraged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: On reinforcing Muslim institutions, the new amendment will allow men to apply for divorce as plaintiffs without pronouncing the talak.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: My question is: will the Syariah Court still require the pronouncement of talak at any point of time to be in accordance with Islamic law in the finalisation of the divorce?

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: If the Muslim man's right to pronounce the talak is recognised under the Act if he still chooses to do so, how does this discourage the frivolous pronouncements of talak outside the Syariah Court?

sections.label: Child care arrangements on divorce
sections.summary: The amendment lets the Syariah Court propose care and living arrangements for a child of the marriage, based on the child's interests, when couples intend to initiate divorce proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The proposed amendment will allow the Syariah Court, amongst others, to propose care and living arrangements for any child of the marriage, based on the child's interests, when there are couples intending to initiate divorce proceedings.

sections.label: Compulsory marriage preparation course
sections.summary: Clause 23 introduces section 94(A), requiring couples in a certain classification to attend and complete a marriage preparation course or programme before applying to a Kadi or Naib Kadi for solemnisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, I would like to touch on clause 23 that introduces section 94(A) which requires any couple that fall within a certain classification to compulsorily attend and complete a marriage preparation course or programme before the couple can apply to a Kadi or Naib Kadi for the solemnisation of their marriage.

sections.label: Majlis powers over wakaf
sections.summary: Clause 16 amends section 58 to enhance the powers of the Majlis to administer any wakaf or nazar am.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Clause 16 amends section 58 to enhance the powers of the Majlis to administer any wakaf or nazar am.

sections.label: MUIS mosque administration powers
sections.summary: Clause 18 amends section 74 to further enhance the powers of MUIS in the administration of every mosque in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Clause 18 amends section 74 to further enhance the powers of MUIS in the administration of every mosque in Singapore.

sections.label: Wakaf jurisdiction and Majlis control
sections.summary: The speaker suggests wakaf and nazar proceedings be decided by the Syariah Court rather than civil Courts, and asks what channels exist for those contesting Majlis decisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, I would like to suggest that proceedings relating to wakaf and nazar be referred to and decided by the Syariah Court and not the civil Courts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: By referring it to the Syariah Court, this will overcome the issue of different jurisdiction and values between the Majlis and civil Courts that may be contradictory.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I feel that the Syariah Court's jurisdiction needs to be widened to include proceedings relating to the issues of wakaf and nazar.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It aims to reinforce institutions and improve the management of Muslim assets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, I do feel some unease with efforts to give the Majlis, as an administrative entity, too much control or full control in the administration of Muslim assets and institutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify, if anyone among those being administered feel unhappy and would like to contest the decision taken by the Majlis on a particular matter, what are the available channels to do so?

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For instance, if there is a trustee or mutawalli whose appointment was removed by the Majlis but felt that the Majlis' decision was excessive and unfair, what action can this individual take?

sections.label: AMLA marriage and divorce amendments
sections.summary: The Bill raises support for minor couples via parental consent and marriage preparation, and adds child-centric guidance for divorcing couples.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I also congratulate the community for reaping the fruits of their contributions over the years to MBMF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I note that AMLA was amended in 2008 to raise the minimum age for marriage from 16 to 18 years of age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The amendments in the Bill today provide for more measures to better support minor couples, including requiring parental consent to the marriage and mandatory participation in a marriage preparation programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We also see an increased child-centric approach in various proposals to enhance guidance for divorcing couples, which is important not just for the Muslim community but for all marriages in Singapore.

sections.label: Muslim Religious Schools Rules
sections.summary: MCCY and MUIS introduced the Administration of Muslim Law (Muslim Religious Schools) Rules, in force since January this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Where necessary, the community has also been more than willing to work closely with the Government to support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I recall that MCCY and MUIS introduced subsidiary legislation, the Administration of Muslim Law (Muslim Religious Schools) Rules, that came into force in January this year.

sections.label: Three-year residence for Muslim divorce
sections.summary: The amendment allows divorce for Muslim couples resident in Singapore at least three years, barring foreign couples who cannot meet this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With this amendment, divorce can take place for Muslim couples who have resided in Singapore for at least three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hence, foreign Muslim couples who cannot fulfil this requirement are automatically not allowed to choose Singapore as the centre for their divorce.

sections.label: Wakaf disputes referred to MUIS
sections.summary: Wakaf disputes previously referred to the High Court will now be referred only to MUIS' office, as wakaf relates to Syariah law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Previously, disputes involving wakaf were usually referred to the High Court, but, now, it will only be referred to MUIS' office.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Because the issue of wakaf is usually related to Syariah law, it is more appropriate for this matter to be administered by an authority like MUIS.

sections.label: Mutawalli appointment for wakaf
sections.summary: The amendment to section 74 concerns appointment of a mutawalli for wakaf management, which requires approval by the authorities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The amendment to section 74 touches on the appointment of a mutawalli for wakaf management, which needs to be approved by the authorities.

sections.label: Hibah and HDB flats
sections.summary: A 11 July 2017 High Court case showed hibah in connection with HDB flats is still not accepted, as HDB rejected the agreement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The final point that I would like to highlight is about hibah in connection with HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There was a case in the High Court dated 11 July 2017 which featured someone who should have inherited an HDB flat in accordance with a hibah agreement, but was rejected by HDB on the basis that the agreement using hibah cannot be accepted by HDB and it contravenes HDB's rules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This clearly showed that hibah in connection with HDB flats is still not accepted.

sections.label: AMLA amendments direction
sections.summary: The amendments to AMLA are described as timely and heading in the right direction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: (In English): The amendments to AMLA are timely and are seen to be taking the path in the right direction.

sections.label: Counselling compliance rate update
sections.summary: It asks for an update on the compliance rate with counselling implemented and conducted under sections 43A and B.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: On section 43A and B, can we be updated on how good the compliance rate is with counselling that has been implemented and conducted thus far?

sections.label: Parenting plan submission criteria
sections.summary: It asks the Minister to update on the criteria required for submitting a parenting plan under new section 46A.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: On the new section 46A, can the Minister update us on what are the criteria required in the submission of the "parenting plan"?

sections.label: Divorce process timelines and KPIs
sections.summary: It asks how timelines and waiting times for divorce processes are kept within set limits and KPIs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The procedures and processes highlighted are a necessity and help keep checks and balances in couples considering divorce.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: However, how do we ensure that the timeline for these processes and waiting times are within certain set limits and KPIs as, very often, we hear of issues and feedback pertaining to the long waiting and processing times which may drag on for months and, in some cases, even years?

sections.label: Expanded use of funds
sections.summary: It asks for an update on the expanded use of funds given the new increased rate payable per month.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: With the new increased rate payable per month, can we get an update on the expanded use of the funds?

sections.label: Multiple marriages in Singapore
sections.summary: It asks how many people in Singapore married more than one wife in the past five years, trends, and divorce rate.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: This is especially so for those who are married more than once or marry more than one wife.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: So far, how many people in Singapore have married more than one wife within the past five years?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Is there a particular trend that can be observed among such marriages and what is the divorce rate for such couples?

sections.label: Maintenance for remarried men
sections.summary: The passage asks what is being done about men who remarried but cannot pay maintenance for ex-wives and children.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: What is being done about the issue of men who remarried but are unable to pay for the maintenance of their ex-wives and children?

sections.label: Bill changes and Islamic tenets
sections.summary: The passage states the Bill's proposed changes are in line with Islamic tenets and move with the times.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The proposed changes in this Bill are in line with Islamic tenets and move with the times.

sections.label: MBMF use for mosques
sections.summary: The passage supports using MBMF monies for mosque maintenance, educational facilities and madrasahs, and asks about buying land to build mosques.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I also support the provision to use MBMF, as stated in clause 19 to amend section 77.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I agree with this provision which enables MBMF monies to be used for mosque maintenance works and educational facilities in these mosques, as well as in full-time madrasahs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, I would also like to ask the Minister whether MBMF can also be used to procure land to build mosques and, if so, is there a prescribed limit, in percentage terms, to use the MBMF monies for this purpose.

sections.label: MENDAKI, SkillsFuture, marriage preparation
sections.summary: The passage says MENDAKI should play a larger role with SkillsFuture and supports requiring under-21s to attend marriage preparation and obtain consent.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Now, with the national movement SkillsFuture, I think MENDAKI should play a larger role to help our community prepare itself to navigate an economy that is more challenging and volatile.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I also support the enactment of section 94, whereby those under the age of 21 must participate in a marriage preparation course and must also obtain consent from their mother, father or an appropriate and legal guardian or wali, before they can register their marriage with a Naib Kadi or Kadi.

sections.label: Support for section 46B divorce intervention
sections.summary: The passage states support for adding section 46B to provide another layer of possible intervention in divorce applications.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: (In English): Madam, I support the addition of section 46B, where the intent is to provide another layer of possible intervention in the application for a divorce.

sections.label: Empowering Syariah Court child assessments
sections.summary: The passage agrees to empower the Syariah Court to appoint professionals to assess children, suggests including teachers or edu-carers, and supports the AMLA amendments.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I agree to empowering the Syariah Court to, I quote, "appoint, in any proceedings involving the custody or welfare of a child, a registered medical practitioner, psychologist, counsellor, social worker, or mental health professional to examine and assess the child for the purposes of preparing expert evidence for use" in Court proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I feel that it is also useful to consider including the child's teachers or edu-carers who see and observe the child's social interactions and personal growth on a regular basis, among this group of professionals tasked to assess the child's mental, emotional and social well-being.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: All in all, I support the amendments proposed to AMLA.

sections.label: Syariah Court jurisdiction amendment
sections.summary: The amendment to section 35 requires a party to be domiciled or habitually resident in Singapore for at least three years before the Syariah Court has jurisdiction.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: One issue relates to the jurisdiction of the Syariah Court.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I welcome the amendment to section 35 to require either party to a marriage to be domiciled in Singapore or habitually resident in Singapore for a period of at least three years before the Syariah Court has jurisdiction to hear matters.

sections.label: High Court financial relief for Muslims
sections.summary: The Court of Appeal in TMO vs TMP found no lacuna in the law and that chapter 4A of the Women's Charter can apply to Muslims.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Parties would typically have to go to the civil Court, the High Court, to obtain the appropriate orders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I note that there had been developments in this matter as the Court of Appeal in the case of TMO vs TMP had found that there is no lacuna in the law and that chapter 4A of the Women's Charter, which empowers the High Court to order financial relief upon divorce granted by competent courts overseas, can apply to Muslims.

sections.label: Syariah Court Inheritance Certificate
sections.summary: The Syariah Court currently issues the Inheritance Certificate upon the provision of a statutory declaration.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Currently, the Syariah Court issues the Inheritance Certificate upon the provision of a statutory declaration.

sections.label: Overseeing inheritance distribution issues
sections.summary: One possible approach is to grant powers to the Syariah Court or create a separate tribunal to oversee inheritance distribution issues.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: One possible approach may be to grant powers to the Syariah Court or create a separate tribunal to oversee the issues relating to the inheritance distribution, including issues relating to the Muslim will, nuzriah, hibah and enforcement of the beneficiaries' duties.

sections.label: AMLA amendment Bill welcomed
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the amendment Bill, which aims to reinforce Islamic institutions, enhance management of Muslim assets and strengthen Muslim families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: (In Malay):   AMLA is an important piece of legislation in the administration of various aspects of life for the Muslim community in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: If we look at the history and development of AMLA, we can see the beauty and uniqueness of the Singapore Story, in which the welfare of the Malay/Muslim community is given attention.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Therefore, I truly welcome this amendment Bill which aims to continue reinforcing Islamic institutions, enhancing the management of Muslim assets and strengthening Muslim families − and, at once, enhancing the unity of the Muslim community in Singapore in general.

sections.label: Complex Muslim community life
sections.summary: The speaker hopes Islamic education efforts continue and that the legislation's application is observed and improved to match today's realities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The reality is that life for those in the Muslim community is becoming increasingly complex and our community needs comprehensive and progressive guidance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I hope that the effort to enhance Islamic education within our community will continue to be given due attention.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: This amendment is certainly a positive step and it is hoped that the application of this legislation will continue to be observed and improvements are done consistently, so that it corresponds with the realities of life in today's society.

sections.label: Section 58(7) wakaf clarification
sections.summary: New section 58(7) is intended as a clarification to section 63 of AMLA on when the Court is brought in.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For example, the new section 58(7), which is intended to be seen as a clarification to section 63 of AMLA which specifies that the Court is only brought in if the Majlis or MUIS finds "the meaning or effect of any instrument or declaration creating or affecting any wakaf or nazar is obscure or uncertain".

sections.label: Trustee removal grounds and recourse
sections.summary: The Member asks whether there is impetus for further grounds to remove a trustee or mutawalli and about other avenues for recourse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In this case, can the Minister share if there has been any specific impetus that has created the need to specify further grounds for removal of a trustee or mutawalli?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In addition, should disputing parties not agree with the Wakaf Dispute Resolution Committee and the eventual decision by the MUIS Council, would they have any other avenues for recourse?

sections.label: Counselling attendance non-compliance consequences
sections.summary: The Member asks whether there are consequences for non-compliance with an order to attend counselling, noting one-attendee sessions are unlikely to help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For example, a marriage counselling session with just one attendee is unlikely to help the couple.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Hence, I would like to ask whether there are consequences for non-compliance of an order to attend counselling.

sections.label: Overseas divorce asset division case
sections.summary: A 2012 Johor divorce left the Singapore Syariah Court without jurisdiction to divide assets, awarding far less than their value.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In February this year, the Straits Times reported a case in which a man had divorced his wife in 2012 in the Johor Syariah Subordinate Court, allegedly without telling her.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: When the woman applied to the Singapore Syariah Court to divide their assets, the Court did not have jurisdiction to do so as it was not the Court that dissolved the marriage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Under Muslim law, it was only able to award her, against her former husband, an amount of maintenance and gift that was far less than the value of the assets that was up for division.

sections.label: Syariah Court overseas divorce orders
sections.summary: The local Syariah Court should be empowered to make orders on ancillary issues pertaining to overseas divorces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The local Syariah Court should be empowered to make orders on ancillary issues pertaining to overseas divorces.

sections.label: Incentives and AMLA amendments welcomed
sections.summary: The Member welcomes the AMLA amendments, especially those protecting children and minors amid rising divorce among young Muslim couples.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Perhaps, offering incentives could help to increase interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I welcome these progressive and timely amendments to AMLA, especially in relation to the amendments that seek to offer greater protection to children and minors in attempting to address the growing rate of divorce amongst young Muslim couples.

sections.label: Child representative protection wording
sections.summary: Section 45(5) of the Family Justice Act 2014 protects a child representative for good faith acts without fraud or wilful misconduct, but clause 15(c) omits the words 'on the part of the child representative'.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In the case of section 45(5) of the Family Justice Act 2014, a child representative there receives protection as long as the act (a) was done in good faith and (b) did not involve any fraud or wilful misconduct on the part of the child representative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, in the case of the proposed amendments in the current Bill, clause 15(c) follows the language of the Family Justice Act 2014, but leaves out the words "on the part of the child representative" after the words "did not involve any fraud or wilful misconduct".

sections.label: Matrimonial property division provision
sections.summary: For division of matrimonial property in Singapore, there is no similar provision in AMLA or the amendments proposed under the current Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In at least one area, dealing with the division of matrimonial property in Singapore, there is no similar provision in AMLA or the amendments proposed under the current Bill.

sections.label: Syariah Court jurisdiction proposal
sections.summary: A proposal is made that further amendments be introduced specifically granting the Syariah Court jurisdiction in such cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can I propose that further amendments be introduced, specifically granting the Syariah Court jurisdiction in such cases?

sections.label: Mandatory marriage education for minor couples
sections.summary: Marriage education programmes tailored for different groups are already available, but attendance is being made mandatory for minor couples as they most require support.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Marriage education programmes tailored for different groups are already available, but we are making it mandatory for minor couples for now as they represent the group that most requires support.

sections.label: Post-divorce consultation for Muslim couples
sections.summary: Divorcing Muslim couples with children up to 21 years old must attend a free two-hour post-divorce consultation session before collecting their divorce certificates.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Third, divorcing Muslim couples with children up to 21 years old are also required to attend a free two-hour post-divorce consultation session before the collection of their divorce certificates.

sections.label: Divorce case completion timelines
sections.summary: If parties are amicable and agree on divorce and ancillary matters, cases can be completed within three to six months, while typically 30% are acrimonious or complex.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: As regards the timelines post-counselling, if the parties are amicable and come to an agreement on the divorce and ancillary matters, their case can be completed within three to six months.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: However, there are typically 30% of cases that are either acrimonious in nature or more complex with multi-faceted issues.

sections.label: Court allows wife's financial relief appeal
sections.summary: The Court allowed the wife's appeal to seek financial relief at the High Court, and the Court of Appeal confirmed there is no lacuna in the law.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: The Court eventually allowed the appeal for the wife to seek financial relief at the High Court, on the basis that chapter 4A of Part X of the Women's Charter can apply to Muslims where necessary.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: More importantly, the Court of Appeal confirmed that there is no lacuna in the law.

sections.label: Wakaf Dispute Resolution Committee by MUIS
sections.summary: MUIS introduced a Wakaf Dispute Resolution Committee to mediate wakaf disputes outside civil Courts, answering Mr Faisal Manap.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: The effort to introduce a Wakaf Dispute Resolution Committee was an innovative but necessary approach by MUIS, to ensure that there are neutral individuals with the necessary expertise to help mediate disputes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: So, to answer Mr Faisal Manap, we do have a scheme to resolve wakaf disputes outside of the civil Courts and this is through the Wakaf Dispute Resolution Committee appointed by MUIS.

sections.label: MUIS uses MBMF for mosque facilities
sections.summary: Since 2009, MUIS has used MBMF to add over 23,200 prayer spaces, build religious class facilities and introduce elderly-friendly and disabled-friendly features.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Since 2009, MUIS has leveraged on MBMF to add over 23,200 prayer spaces, build more religious class facilities and introduced more elderly-friendly and disabled-friendly features.

sections.label: MUIS approves MBMF works judiciously
sections.summary: MUIS will continue to use MBMF judiciously and will only approve necessary or useful works for mosques and full-time madrasahs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: MUIS will continue to ensure that MBMF is used judiciously and, to this end, will only approve necessary or useful works for our mosques and full-time madrasahs.

sections.label: Rules came into force
sections.summary: The Rules came into force on 1 January this year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: The Rules came into force on 1 January this year.

sections.label: Marriage preparation and Syariah Court powers
sections.summary: A compulsory marriage preparation programme starts with minor couples, requiring parental consent, and the Syariah Court's jurisdiction and powers are expanded.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: However, marriages involving minor couples are still vulnerable to higher risks.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Therefore, a compulsory marriage preparation programme will be introduced, starting with minor couples.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Parents or guardians must give consent before the couple can register to be married.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Nonetheless, we must increase our efforts to prevent a rising trend of divorces.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Therefore, the Syariah Court's jurisdiction will be expanded to ensure that couples who wish to divorce attend the Marriage Counselling Programme.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: The Syariah Court will also be given powers to appoint an expert who will represent the interests of a child whose parents are undergoing a divorce.

sections.label: Syariah Court residency and wakaf revenue
sections.summary: Cases are heard only if one party has habitually resided in Singapore for three consecutive years, and in 2016 MUIS distributed over $3 million of wakaf revenue.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Third, in order to ensure that the Syariah Court's resources are used optimally, cases will be heard only if at least one party filing the application is habitually residing in Singapore for a period of at least three consecutive years.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: In 2016, MUIS distributed over $3 million of revenue generated from wakaf properties to mosques, madrasahs and Muslim organisations.

sections.label: Discomfort over pantun and AMLA Bill
sections.summary: A Muslim Member felt discomfort at the pantun and notes the AMLA Bill's amendments involved MUIS, MCCY and Muslim community feedback.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
sentences.text: As a Member of the Muslim community and a practising Muslim, I had a lot of discomfort listening to that pantun and I really want to understand the meaning behind it or the intended meaning.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
sentences.text: We know that the AMLA Bill has been put forth with amendments with a lot of work from MUIS, as well as MCCY, and the members of the Muslim community who have given feedback.

sections.label: Question on MUIS and Syariah Court injustice
sections.summary: Mr Faisal Manap is asked if anything in the amendment Bill could lead to MUIS or the Syariah Court acting unjustly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
sentences.text: Is there anything in the amendment Bill which Mr Faisal Manap feels could lead to MUIS or the Syariah Court being unjust in their actions?

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
sentences.text: But I think, in the pantun, it does say that we have to answer to the higher authority if we are unjust in this world.

sections.label: Agreement on amendments' spirit
sections.summary: Mr Faisal Manap is asked whether he agrees the Bill's amendments are in the spirit of the Muslim community acting in good faith.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
sentences.text: Would Mr Faisal Manap then agree that the amendments made in the Bill are in the spirit of the Muslim community, acting in good faith of what is in the best for the community?
